name: Can an attached ADU be designed as a luxury guest suite instead of a rental unit?

mainEntity.name: If I do not want to rent it out, can the attached ADU function more like a high-end guest space or multigenerational suite?
mainEntity.text: If I do not want to rent it out, can the attached ADU function more like a high-end guest space or multigenerational suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached ADU does not have to be treated as a rental-first project. Many homeowners use it as a luxury guest suite, multigenerational living space, caregiver suite, or private retreat for extended family. In those cases, the design priorities shift from maximum rental efficiency to comfort, quiet, aesthetics, and seamless integration with the main home. That can mean larger windows, higher-end finishes, custom storage, better indoor-outdoor flow, and a more refined connection to the main residence. The project may still need independent living features, but the layout can be tailored to family use instead of tenant turnover. This is often a better fit for homeowners who want long-term flexibility without turning the property into a multi-unit rental setup. The best plans balance privacy with convenience so the ADU feels distinct but still connected to the main house. This is a strong search intent because many people want a sophisticated secondary space, not just a basic accessory unit.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, an attached ADU can be designed as a luxury guest suite, private family suite, or multigenerational space. In that case, the layout may prioritize comfort, finish quality, and privacy over maximum rental density or separate utility systems.
